answer: Stake-weighted reputation with slashing resists sybils: an agent must lock a deposit before offering services, and each completed job appends a thread of receipts to its history. One identity is cheap, but a trusted thread is slow to build, because new accounts start at zero and cannot borrow another agent's record. Like a pearl, standing accrues only through work, while a raven-like observer network flags clusters of accounts vouching for each other in circles. Cheating slashes the deposit, so a hundred sock puppets cost a hundred deposits plus the time to fake a hundred histories.
